solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Expert left out of deception (4)

indicators.note: 'left out of' literally says L (left) is omitted from the word that follows

blocks.note: a bluff is a deception, a pretence of strength
L = left, the letter taken out

annotation.surface: An expert who has been kept out of some deceit.
annotation.walkthrough: A buff is an enthusiast who knows a subject inside out, as in a film buff.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a buff, like a history buff, is an enthusiast expert in a subject.

entries.clue: President’s youngest child, cute little creature (8)

blocks.note: the baby of the family is its youngest child

annotation.surface: A President's youngest child described as adorable.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it look as if the child belongs to the President; in fact it just joins the two parts.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: the bushbaby is a small, huge-eyed African primate that most people find cute.

entries.clue: Pupils team up in a methodical way (8)

blocks.note: a form is a school class, a group of pupils

annotation.surface: Schoolchildren pairing up in an orderly fashion.
annotation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group, so 'pupils' gives FORM.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something formally means following set procedure step by step, which is to be methodical.

entries.clue: Brochure mistakenly supports involving European Commission (10)

indicators.note: something done mistakenly is done wrong, so the letters of 'supports' are put in the wrong order
to involve is to include or take in, so the scrambled letters take EC inside them

annotation.surface: A brochure that wrongly claims to back a Brussels body.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supports' reads as a verb, but it is only the letters to be scrambled, and the Brussels body is dropped into the middle of them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a prospectus is a printed brochure describing a school, company or share offer.

entries.clue: Wine and port meets with Hamburg sommelier’s approval (5)

blocks.note: ja is German for yes, what a sommelier in Hamburg would say

annotation.surface: A wine-and-port pairing wins the nod from a German wine waiter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as a second drink next to wine, but it is the city of Rio.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Rioja is a Spanish wine, usually red, named after its region.

entries.clue: Tweeter’s mostly drunken gossip (9)

indicators.note: 'mostly' means most but not all, so the next word loses its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone on social media posting half-drunk tittle-tattle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tweeter' suggests a social media user; here it is a songbird, and the 's means 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning description: the stonechat is a small European songbird, and birds tweet.

entries.clue: Formation of the ruling class (13)

blocks.note: the act of founding or setting something up
the powerful elite, usually with a capital letter

annotation.surface: How a ruling elite comes into being.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, but 'of' only joins two separate meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the founding of something, and the entrenched elite known as the Establishment.

entries.clue: Bishop intervening in case concerning family (6)

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so B comes between the letters of the next word

blocks.note: a court case is a trial

annotation.surface: A bishop getting involved in a family court case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a container indicator, but it is the thing being entered, a court case.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose sense: a tribe is a large extended family group, so tribal matters concern family.

entries.clue: Perhaps Pedro Ximénez reluctant to welcome European bishop (6)

indicators.note: to welcome guests is to take them in, so the first word takes the others inside it

blocks.note: RR = Right Reverend, a bishop's title

annotation.surface: A Spanish-sounding man hesitant to host a visiting prelate.
annotation.walkthrough: Pedro Ximénez looks like a person but is a grape and its wine, and 'Perhaps' marks it as one example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Pedro Ximénez is the dark, sweet sherry made from the grape of that name.

entries.clue: A blow if French business has to absorb most of shock (7)

indicators.note: to absorb is to soak up and hold inside, so the letters before it take the shortened word in
most but not all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to rock = to shock; drop the K

annotation.surface: A French firm takes a hit when forced to soak up a shock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A blow' looks like a setback but is a wind; the French and business parts sit either side of the inserted piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful sense: the sirocco is a hot wind off North Africa, and a wind is a blow.

entries.clue: Joining European race with Italian chap in the lead (13)

indicators.note: a runner in the lead is out in front, so these pieces go at the start

blocks.note: a race or people is a nation

annotation.surface: An Italian man leading some European contest, which he enters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian chap' is not a unit: 'with Italian' is one piece and 'chap' another, and both go at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: to concatenate is to link things together like a chain (Latin catena), so the noun is a joining.

entries.clue: Divulged policy’s main points (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is a singular noun; 'main points' describes what it contains

blocks.note: once divulged, a secret is out
a party line is a policy; the 's means 'is'

annotation.surface: A leaked summary of government policy.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possession but links wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: an outline is a summary that gives only the main points.

entries.clue: Head of brotherhood drops rash idea (9)

indicators.note: the head of something is its top or front, so take the first letter of 'brotherhood'

blocks.note: a rash of burglaries is a wave of them

annotation.surface: A fraternity leader abandons a reckless plan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drops' and 'rash' read as verb and adjective; both are nouns here.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific kind: a brainwave is a sudden bright idea.

entries.clue: When caught, clamour for PM (5)

indicators.note: a sound is caught by the ear, so this means 'when heard'

blocks.note: a blare is a loud clamour, as of trumpets

annotation.surface: A noisy demand that the Prime Minister be arrested.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught' suggests an arrest or C for caught; here it means heard. Tony Blair was UK Prime Minister 1997-2007.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Tony Blair was Britain's Prime Minister (PM) from 1997 to 2007.

entries.clue: Romantic song sequence enthralling new spouse? (4,3,5)

indicators.note: to enthral is literally to hold captive, so the song holds N inside it

blocks.note: a ballad is a romantic song
a chain of events is a sequence

annotation.surface: A love song cycle that captivates someone just married.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a jokey definition: the phrase is unflattering slang for a wife or husband, pictured as a prisoner's shackle.
annotation.definitionFit: Humorous slang: a ball and chain is a convict's shackle, used jokingly of the spouse who ties one down.

entries.clue: Gun going astray in revolutionary socialist’s possession (9)

indicators.note: a revolution is a turn, so the socialist is turned round
'in' places one piece inside another
what one possesses one holds, so the turned socialist holds the other piece

annotation.surface: A gun that has gone missing, found in the hands of a left-wing radical.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary socialist' reads as one phrase, a political firebrand; 'revolutionary' is actually the instruction to turn the socialist round.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific kind: a derringer is a small pocket pistol, named after its American maker Henry Deringer.

entries.clue: Chained off area in Mexican plantation (8)

indicators.note: something off is not right or has gone bad, so the letters are out of order

annotation.surface: A roped-off section of a Mexican estate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chained off area' reads as a fenced zone; 'off' is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional word: hacienda is Spanish for a large estate or plantation, especially in Mexico.

entries.clue: Usher periodically wangles cheap accommodation (8)

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so take every other letter

blocks.note: to usher someone is to steer them

annotation.surface: An usher who keeps fiddling bargain-basement rooms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Usher' is a verb here, not the person at the door.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical sense: steerage was the cheapest passenger class on a ship, near the rudder.

entries.clue: Might it indicate a revealing exchange? (5-2-5)

annotation.definition: Might it indicate a revealing exchange?

blocks.note: the plain reading: a talk in which feelings are revealed
the setter's twist: read literally, an exchange from one heart to another, as in a transplant

annotation.surface: Wondering whether something hints at a candid talk.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is the ordinary phrase for a frank talk, but read literally it describes swapping one heart for another, the surgical exchange the question half-suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a heart-to-heart is an intimate conversation in which feelings are laid bare.

entries.clue: Part of rifle butt (6)

blocks.note: the tube the bullet travels along
a butt is also a large cask, for wine or beer

annotation.surface: The wooden stock at the back of a rifle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rifle butt' reads as one thing, the shoulder end of a gun; split it, and butt means a cask.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the tube of a gun, and a large cask, which is what a butt is.

entries.clue: On which one may speak of dishonour, quietly at first (6)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a descriptive phrase for the noun

indicators.note: what comes at first comes before everything else, so the quiet letter goes at the front

annotation.surface: A speaker quietly raising a matter of disgrace.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speak of dishonour' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'speak', and 'of' only links it to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a podium is a raised platform on which a speaker stands to address an audience.

entries.clue: Nothing dividing city assembly (5)

indicators.note: to divide something is to split it in two, so O splits the city's name by sitting inside it

blocks.note: the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

annotation.surface: A town council that can agree on nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'City assembly' reads as a town council; the city is only wordplay and 'assembly' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical sense: in ancient Greek cities the agora was the public assembly and the square it met in.

entries.clue: New realities for Hebrew (9)

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A changed world for the Hebrew language.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hebrew' looks like the language; here it is a person.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym in the historical sense: a Hebrew is a member of the ancient Jewish people of Israel.

entries.clue: Always around, guarding English official from past (5)

indicators.note: turned around, so the word is written backwards
a guard surrounds what it protects, so the reversed word surrounds E

annotation.surface: A historical English officer who was always on guard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around' could mean containing, but here it turns the word round, and 'guarding' does the containing.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical sense: a reeve was a local official in medieval England, surviving in sheriff (shire-reeve).

entries.clue: Protesting Republican in a bad way (7)

annotation.surface: A sickly Republican complaining loudly.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer reads first as a fence; here it is the verb rail, to protest bitterly.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to rail against something is to protest about it angrily.

entries.clue: State school accepting society backing ChatGPT among others (7)

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the school takes S inside it
going backwards, so the AI letters are reversed

blocks.note: Eton College, the famous English boarding school
ChatGPT is one of many AIs

annotation.surface: A state school embraces a society that supports ChatGPT and the like.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State school' reads as a state-funded school; 'State' alone is the definition, and Eton is famously private.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Estonia is one of the three Baltic states, a sovereign country.

entries.clue: Prominent figures rattled Mailer in US (10)

indicators.note: something rattled is shaken up, so the letters are mixed

annotation.surface: Celebrities unsettled the novelist Norman Mailer in America.
annotation.walkthrough: Norman Mailer, the American novelist, makes 'rattled' look like a verb with celebrities as its subject.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: luminaries are people who shine in their field, eminent figures.

entries.clue: Assistant’s final check (4)

blocks.note: a helper to a tradesman, as in a plumber's helper
in chess, the check that ends the game

annotation.surface: An assistant doing the last inspection.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Final check' looks like an inspection; it is checkmate. The 's means 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a tradesman's helper, as in a builder's mate, and short for checkmate.
